producer_report.summary: Readings are now checked against the boundary words and the repo's files at the base commit. Root cause: `check_reading_acceptance` checked only the previous result and scope, criterion evidence, the code survey and governance files. It never compared the reading's text with the boundary word list or its deliverables with the files at HEAD. A new `check_boundary_and_repo_files` in reading.rs runs last in that function, with the root cause in its doc comment. It scans the title, summary, reasons, question, departures, assumptions, out-of-scope items, criteria, default notes and deliverable paths with `athena_context::briefs::boundary_scan`. The error names each field and word. With the file list it also refuses a modify or delete of an absent path (a directory with files under it counts as present), and a create of a path that is already a file. A modify of an absent CHANGELOG.md is allowed, because Athena adds that deliverable itself. Paths are judged only for a reading with a capability and no open question. `check_reading_acceptance` gains a `repo_files: Option<&BTreeSet<String>>` argument. `read_once` passes the set from `git.ls_tree(&jc.commit)`. `check_reading_text` (the `athena check-reading` replay) passes `None`, so it checks words only. The refusal goes back to the reader once through the existing path. New tests: unit tests in reading.rs for words and paths, and three reader-path tests in run_pin_tests.rs (a dirty summary on both reads; an absent path on the first read, then corrected; an absent path on both reads). Three fixtures broke and were fixed so each still tests what it was written for. The fake reader now returns `modify` when its workdir already holds FAKE-CHANGE.md; a unit test covers this. The drain.rs plan test now commits the file before the reading and removes it afterwards. The steward.rs nested-run test no longer deletes README.md. A CHANGELOG.md entry records it, with the 5% newly-refused estimate (an estimate, not measured).

checks_run.note: 613 passed in athena-core, including the new reading.rs and run_pin_tests.rs tests; athena-agent 43 passed

The first run failed in drain.rs and steward.rs. After the fixture fixes, drain (100 tests) passed; steward (10 tests) passed in a separate run. The athena-cli run that showed the steward failure had every other binary passing.

criteria_check.criterion: Root cause is named in the CHANGELOG.md entry and in a doc comment: reading output was checked only for prior-result, evidence, survey and governance rules, not against the boundary word list or repo files at HEAD. The check is called from check_reading_acceptance in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, not in a prompt file.
criteria_check.evidence: Read the diff. The doc comment on `check_boundary_and_repo_files` and the new CHANGELOG.md entry both state the root cause. `check_reading_acceptance` calls the check as its last line. No prompt file was touched.

criteria_check.criterion: A unit test in reading.rs fails without the change and passes with it: a reading whose summary holds a boundary-scan word is refused and the error names the word. Run `cargo test -p athena-core reading`.
criteria_check.evidence: Test `a_reading_whose_summary_holds_a_boundary_word_is_refused_and_the_word_is_named` calls `check_reading_acceptance` with a summary holding a word built from pieces. It asserts `unwrap_err()` and that the message names the word and `summary`. Without the check the call returns Ok, so `unwrap_err` panics. `a_boundary_word_in_any_text_field_or_path_is_refused_with_the_field_named` covers the other fields, a path fragment and a deliverable path. Both pass in `cargo test --locked -p athena-core`.

criteria_check.criterion: A unit test shows a 'modify' or 'delete' deliverable for a path absent at HEAD is refused, a 'create' deliverable for an existing path is refused, and a reading with valid paths and clean text is accepted. Run `cargo test -p athena-core reading`.
criteria_check.evidence: Test `a_deliverable_that_disagrees_with_the_files_at_head_is_refused` covers modify and delete of docs/missing.md (refused, path named), create of README.md (refused), and a valid modify plus create (accepted). `the_path_rule_allows_a_directory_and_an_absent_changelog_and_skips_without_a_file_set` covers directories, the CHANGELOG.md exemption and the `None` skip. Both pass.

criteria_check.criterion: A test drives the reader path with the fake reader returning a bad reading and shows the reading is not accepted and the reason reaches the caller. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria_check.evidence: run_pin_tests.rs has `a_reading_with_a_boundary_word_is_not_accepted_and_the_word_reaches_the_caller` and `a_reading_that_names_an_absent_file_twice_is_the_failure_and_the_path_reaches_the_caller`. Both go through `Athena::ask` with a fake reader tweak. `reading` is None, `reader_error` names the word or path, and the reader ran twice. `a_reading_naming_a_file_absent_at_head_is_read_again_and_a_corrected_one_is_accepted` shows the second brief carries the refusal and a corrected reading is accepted. All pass in `cargo test -p athena-core`.

criteria_check.criterion: Existing reading tests, including prior-result and scope tests, still pass; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` all pass.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks for the recorded fmt, clippy and full test results. I ran fmt --check and clippy -D warnings (clean). athena-core, athena-agent, athena-cli (drain and steward after the fixture fixes) and the other crates all pass; the policy scan passes. The existing reading tests changed only by the added `None` argument.

criteria_check.criterion: The change refuses more readings and the higher refusal rate is intended: expected 5% of newly refused readings.
criteria_check.evidence: The refusal tests above show readings the old gate accepted now refused. The CHANGELOG.md entry states the higher refusal rate is intended and gives 5% as an estimate, not measured.

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry saying readings are now checked against the boundary words and the repo's files, written for an outside reader.
criteria_check.evidence: Read CHANGELOG.md. A new first entry under [Unreleased] / Added opens with 'A check of every reading's text against the boundary words, and of its deliverables against the repository's files', in plain words, with no banned word. The policy scan passes.

open_issues: Departures from the plan (the plan listed the fake.rs and drain.rs edits as conditional): fake.rs and drain.rs were needed, as expected. steward.rs was a failing fixture the plan did not predict. Its nested-run test deleted README.md while the default fake reading modifies it, so five jobs in one repo now fail. I removed the `scenario.edits` override and the now-unused `mut`; the test still runs five nested jobs and asserts no model call for the steward.
The 5% newly-refused rate is an estimate and was not measured.
`athena check-reading` replay now also refuses an old stored reading that holds a banned word, though it skips path checks. The replay of accepted readings in the existing tests still passes.
mistakes: The first full `cargo test` run stopped at the first failing binary, so the steward.rs failure showed up only on the `--no-fail-fast` rerun. Cost: one extra test run.
learnings: The reader's workdir is a plain copy of the base commit, deleted before the reading is checked. The check therefore uses `git ls-tree` on the base commit.
Requests holding a banned word are already refused at admission (`refuse_banned_input`), so a reading never needs one.

The deterministic fake reader (athena-agent fake.rs) always returned `create` for FAKE-CHANGE.md. A second landed fake job in one repo would be refused by the new rule, so the fake now returns `modify` when its workdir holds the file.
`cargo test` stops at the first failing test binary; use `--no-fail-fast` to see every failing fixture.
Bash here cannot pipe or tail, and tool-result files are outside the working directory. Use `--quiet` to keep test output short.
desires: A way to read a long tool result saved outside the working directory, or to run tests with filtered output, would have saved a rerun.
